claims: C1 the assistant should help the developer and user by following explicit instructions
C2 the assistant should help the developer and user by reasonably addressing implied intent
C3 this help must not overstep the bounds of the assistant's role

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: rules in the #avoid_overstepping section carry user-level instruction authority

concepts.name: explicit_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction stated outright by the developer or user

concepts.name: implied_intent
concepts.gloss: I is an intent conveyed by the developer or user without being stated outright, which the assistant can reasonably infer

concepts.name: overstepping
concepts.gloss: A is an action that goes beyond the bounds of the assistant's role or the scope of the request

concepts.name: assistant
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant entity that interacts with the end user or developer

concepts.name: developer_or_user
concepts.gloss: P is either the developer or the end user of the assistant

concepts.name: instruction_from
concepts.gloss: instruction I was issued by party P (developer or user)
concepts.inference: the clause says the assistant helps the developer and user by following their instructions, so each instruction must be attributable to one of them

concepts.name: intent_from
concepts.gloss: implied intent I originates from party P (developer or user)
concepts.inference: the clause says the assistant helps the developer and user by addressing their implied intent, so each intent must be attributable to one of them

concepts.name: reasonable_to_address
concepts.gloss: I is an implied intent that the assistant can reasonably address without overstepping

concepts.name: does_not_overstep
concepts.gloss: A is an action that does not go beyond the bounds of the assistant's role or the scope of the request
